result.topic_en: Euler sets up an elastic lamina fixed in a wall at one end, slightly bent from its natural straight state, defines abscissa, ordinate, mass elements and radius of curvature, and derives the bending moment $Kcc\,ddy/dx^2$ that a force at the free end must supply to maintain the curvature.
result.transcription:
450 DE MOTV VIBRATORIO

Tab. VII. Fig. 1.
II. Sit igitur A B huiusmodi lamina elaſtica, altero termino A a muro ſeu parieti immobili infixa, quae deinde a viribus quotcunque incuruata ſit in ſtatum A Y F, quam minime a ſtatu naturali A B diſcrepantem, quoniam enim hic de vibrationibus minimis quaeſtio inſtituitur, curua A Y F tam parum a recta A B ceu axe recedere eſt ſumenda, vt omnes applicatae X Y ſint quaſi infinite paruae, et dum lamina motu vibratorio agitatur, ſingula eius puncta Y ſecundum ipſas applicatas X Y, ſiue accedendo ad axem, ſiue inde recedendo moueantur. Hinc ſi abſciſſa a termino B computata vocetur $BX = x$ et applicata $XY = y$, quoniam haec vt infinite parua ſpectatur, ipſe arcus F Y abſciſſae $BX = x$ aequalis cenſeri poterit, quemadmodum etiam arcus A Y rectae A X aequalis cenſetur. Hinc portionis laminae F Y maſſa ſeu pondus erit $= \frac{Kx}{k}$, eiusque elementi ponduſculum $\frac{Kdx}{k}$, ac ſi longitudinem huius laminae vocemus $BA = a$, eius maſſa ſeu pondus erit $\frac{Ka}{k}$. Praeterea ex formulis notiſſimis radii oſculi Y R in puncto Y ſurſum vergentis valor eſt $r = \frac{ds^3}{dx\,ddy}$, denotante $ds$ elementum curuae, quod quum ſit aequale elemento abſciſſae $dx$, radius iſte oſculi $YR = r$ erit $= \frac{dx^2}{ddy}$, hincque momentum huic curuaturae debitum erit $= \frac{Kcc\,ddy}{dx^2}$. Scilicet ſi in F applicata concipiatur vis quaepiam $Ff$, ea tanta eſſe debet, vt eius momentum reſpectu puncti Y fiat $= \frac{Kcc\,ddy}{dx^2}$, tum enim iſta vis hanc curuaturam conſeruare valebit.

III.

items.quote: radius iſte oſculi $YR = r$ erit $= \frac{dx^2}{ddy}$, hincque momentum huic curuaturae debitum erit $= \frac{Kcc\,ddy}{dx^2}$
items.english: this radius of osculation YR = r will be dx^2/ddy, and hence the moment due to this curvature will be Kcc ddy/dx^2.

items.quote: ſi in F applicata concipiatur vis quaepiam $Ff$, ea tanta eſſe debet, vt eius momentum reſpectu puncti Y fiat $= \frac{Kcc\,ddy}{dx^2}$, tum enim iſta vis hanc curuaturam conſeruare valebit.
items.english: If some force Ff is conceived applied at F, it must be so large that its moment with respect to point Y equals Kcc ddy/dx^2; for then this force will be able to maintain this curvature.
